concept.description: Identify the application's base package: the package that directly contains a type annotated with @SpringBootApplication or @Modulithic. Spring Modulith derives the whole module structure relative to this package, so it is the anchor for convention-based module detection. The package is labelled :Modulith:BasePackage. A project may have more than one (e.g. several Spring Boot apps in one build); each is handled independently.
concept.cypher: MATCH (p:Package)-[:CONTAINS]->(t:Type)-[:ANNOTATED_BY]->(:Annotation)-[:OF_TYPE]->(at:Type) WHERE at.fqn IN [ "org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication", "org.springframework.modulith.Modulithic" ] SET p:Modulith:BasePackage RETURN count(DISTINCT p) AS BasePackages

concept.description: Mark every package that sits directly below a :Modulith:BasePackage as a :Modulith:Module. This is Spring Modulith's default rule: each direct sub-package of the application base package is an application module, whether or not it carries an explicit @ApplicationModule annotation. The module's display name defaults to the (simple) package name; an explicit annotation can override it later (see SpringModulithModuleDisplayName).
concept.cypher: MATCH (base:Modulith:BasePackage)-[:CONTAINS]->(m:Package) SET m:Modulith:Module SET m.modulithDisplayName = coalesce(m.modulithDisplayName, m.name) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS ConventionModules

concept.description: Mark every package whose package-info is annotated with @ApplicationModule as a :Modulith:Module, independent of the base-package convention. This covers modules declared explicitly (e.g. nested or relocated module packages) and also makes the rule set useful for projects scanned without a discoverable @SpringBootApplication class. Runs in addition to, and idempotently with, the convention-based detection. The annotation is reached through the synthetic package-info :Type, not the :Package node (see header note).
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Package)-[:CONTAINS]->(pi:Type)-[:ANNOTATED_BY]->(:Annotation)-[:OF_TYPE]->(at:Type) WHERE pi.name = "package-info" AND at.fqn = "org.springframework.modulith.ApplicationModule" SET m:Modulith:Module SET m.modulithDisplayName = coalesce(m.modulithDisplayName, m.name) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS AnnotatedModules

concept.description: Override modulithDisplayName from the @ApplicationModule(displayName = "...") attribute when present and non-blank. Best-effort: relies on the scanner exposing the scalar annotation attribute as (:Annotation)-[:HAS]->(:Value {name:"displayName"}) with a `value` property; if the shape differs or the attribute is absent, the convention-derived name from the previous concepts is left in place.
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Modulith:Module)-[:CONTAINS]->(pi:Type)-[:ANNOTATED_BY]->(av:Annotation)-[:OF_TYPE]->(at:Type) WHERE pi.name = "package-info" AND at.fqn = "org.springframework.modulith.ApplicationModule" MATCH (av)-[:HAS]->(v:Value {name: "displayName"}) WHERE v.value IS NOT NULL AND trim(toString(v.value)) <> "" SET m.modulithDisplayName = toString(v.value) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS NamedModules

concept.description: Materialize module ownership of types: for every :Modulith:Module, link it to all types nested anywhere beneath it via (:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(:Type). This single relationship lets downstream concepts (exposure, boundary classification) avoid repeated variable-length CONTAINS traversals. Assumes modules are not nested (Spring Modulith's default: sub-packages of a module are internals, not modules); with nested modules a type beneath an inner module would be owned by both, which the boundary concepts do not special-case. Synthetic package-info :Types are excluded — they carry package metadata, not module API.
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Modulith:Module)-[:CONTAINS*1..]->(t:Type) WHERE t.name <> "package-info" MERGE (m)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(t) RETURN count(DISTINCT t) AS OwnedTypes

concept.description: Default named interface: public types located directly in a module's root package form the module's public API. Mark them :Modulith:Exposed and link via :MODULITH_EXPOSES. Types in deeper sub-packages are internal unless a named interface promotes them (see the following concepts). Visibility is taken from the scanner's `visibility` property; types without an explicit public visibility are treated as internal.
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Modulith:Module)-[:CONTAINS]->(t:Type) WHERE t.visibility = "public" SET t:Modulith:Exposed MERGE (m)-[:MODULITH_EXPOSES]->(t) RETURN count(DISTINCT t) AS DefaultExposedTypes

concept.description: Type-level named interface: a type directly annotated with @NamedInterface is part of its owning module's public API regardless of which sub-package it lives in. Mark it :Modulith:Exposed and link via :MODULITH_EXPOSES to its owning module.
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(t:Type)-[:ANNOTATED_BY]->(:Annotation)-[:OF_TYPE]->(at:Type) WHERE at.fqn = "org.springframework.modulith.NamedInterface" SET t:Modulith:Exposed MERGE (m)-[:MODULITH_EXPOSES]->(t) RETURN count(DISTINCT t) AS NamedInterfaceTypes

concept.description: Package-level named interface: when a sub-package's package-info is annotated with @NamedInterface, all public types directly in that package become part of the owning module's public API. The annotation is reached through the package-info :Type, not the :Package node. Mark them :Modulith:Exposed and link via :MODULITH_EXPOSES.
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(t:Type) MATCH (pkg:Package)-[:CONTAINS]->(t) MATCH (pkg)-[:CONTAINS]->(pi:Type)-[:ANNOTATED_BY]->(:Annotation)-[:OF_TYPE]->(at:Type) WHERE pi.name = "package-info" AND at.fqn = "org.springframework.modulith.NamedInterface" AND t.visibility = "public" SET t:Modulith:Exposed MERGE (m)-[:MODULITH_EXPOSES]->(t) RETURN count(DISTINCT t) AS NamedInterfacePackageTypes

concept.description: Materialize declared dependency rules: for each module whose @ApplicationModule declares a non-empty allowedDependencies list, link it to each referenced module via :MODULITH_ALLOWS. Entries of the form "moduleName :: namedInterface" are reduced to their module-name part. Best-effort and the most scanner-shape-dependent concept here: it assumes the array attribute is exposed as (:Annotation)-[:HAS]->(:Value:Array {name:"allowedDependencies"})-[:CONTAINS]->(:Value) and matches the entry against a module's simple name or display name. The @ApplicationModule annotation is reached through the package-info :Type, not the :Package node. A module that declares no allowedDependencies is treated as unrestricted (Spring Modulith's default), so it produces no :MODULITH_ALLOWS edges and is exempt from the allowed-dependency violation check.
concept.cypher: MATCH (m:Modulith:Module)-[:CONTAINS]->(pi:Type)-[:ANNOTATED_BY]->(av:Annotation)-[:OF_TYPE]->(at:Type) WHERE pi.name = "package-info" AND at.fqn = "org.springframework.modulith.ApplicationModule" MATCH (av)-[:HAS]->(:Value {name: "allowedDependencies"})-[:CONTAINS]->(e) WITH m, trim(split(toString(e.value), "::")[0]) AS allowedName WHERE allowedName <> "" MATCH (target:Modulith:Module) WHERE target.name = allowedName OR target.modulithDisplayName = allowedName MERGE (m)-[:MODULITH_ALLOWS]->(target) RETURN count(*) AS AllowedEdges

concept.description: Tag every type-level DEPENDS_ON edge whose endpoints belong to two different modules with modulithCrossModule = true. This is the raw signal the Hierograph dependency provider can aggregate to module level; the two violation concepts then refine a subset of these edges into boundary violations. Edges within a single module, or touching types outside any module, are left untagged.
concept.cypher: MATCH (s:Type)-[r:DEPENDS_ON]->(t:Type) MATCH (m1:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(s) MATCH (m2:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(t) WHERE m1 <> m2 SET r.modulithCrossModule = true RETURN count(*) AS CrossModuleDependencies

concept.description: EXPERIMENTAL — produces false positives because the exposed set ignores @NamedInterface propagation; not in the default group. See the experimental-group comment above. Encapsulation violation: a cross-module dependency that reaches a type which is NOT part of the target module's public API (not :Modulith:Exposed). This is the core Spring Modulith rule — a module may only be accessed through its named interfaces — and holds regardless of any allowedDependencies declaration. Tags the edge with modulithViolation = true and modulithViolationKind = "ENCAPSULATION".
concept.cypher: MATCH (s:Type)-[r:DEPENDS_ON]->(t:Type) WHERE r.modulithCrossModule = true AND NOT t:Modulith:Exposed SET r.modulithViolation = true, r.modulithViolationKind = "ENCAPSULATION" RETURN count(*) AS EncapsulationViolations

concept.description: EXPERIMENTAL — only models allowedDependencies at module granularity (it ignores the named-interface part of entries like "care :: Suggestion Factory"); not in the default group. Disallowed-dependency violation: a cross-module dependency whose source module restricts its dependencies (declares a non-empty allowedDependencies, i.e. has at least one :MODULITH_ALLOWS edge) but the target module is not among the allowed ones. This holds even when the target type is a legitimately exposed named interface — the access itself is not permitted by the declared rules. Tags modulithViolation = true and sets modulithViolationKind to "DISALLOWED_DEPENDENCY" unless the edge was already classified as an ENCAPSULATION violation, which takes precedence.
concept.cypher: MATCH (s:Type)-[r:DEPENDS_ON]->(t:Type) WHERE r.modulithCrossModule = true MATCH (m1:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(s) MATCH (m2:Modulith:Module)-[:MODULITH_OWNS]->(t) WHERE EXISTS { (m1)-[:MODULITH_ALLOWS]->(:Modulith:Module) } AND NOT EXISTS { (m1)-[:MODULITH_ALLOWS]->(m2) } SET r.modulithViolation = true, r.modulithViolationKind = coalesce(r.modulithViolationKind, "DISALLOWED_DEPENDENCY") RETURN count(*) AS AllowedDependencyViolations
